role: Main-actor singleton that owns CloudKit session sync state, account-change handling, the direct per-recording upload path, forwarders to the pull/deletion/scrub/trash-restore coordinators, and the full-sync orchestration with stuck-sync recovery and no-progress watchdog.
types: CloudKitSyncManager: class (@Observable @MainActor final) — CloudKit HRV session sync manager singleton
CloudKitSyncManager.SyncState: enum — idle / syncing / error(String) shown by the sync status UI
toplevel: static let shared = CloudKitSyncManager() builds the singleton lazily with defaults from AppDependencies.current (settingsManager, sessionArchive). Stored initializers: syncState .idle, schemaUnavailable false, lastSyncProgressAt .distantPast, pullVersion 0, container CKContainer(identifier: AppConfig.iCloudContainerIdentifier), recordType "HRVSession", zoneID HRVSessions/current user, syncSerializer SyncSerializer(), observers NotificationTokens(), didBootSyncState lock(false). liveBackup is a lazy CloudKitLiveBackupManager whose ensureZone closure calls ensureZoneExists on the manager.

flags.text: Quarantine is documented as surfaced to the user and reversible (quarantinedCount, quarantinedSessionIds, retryQuarantined), but no code in the repo (app or tests) reads quarantinedCount/quarantinedSessionIds or calls retryQuarantined. A session quarantined by handlePrepFailure is excluded from every push forever and the user is never told it is not backed up.

flags.text: forceReuploadSession mutates state outside syncSerializer (588), unlike markSessionsForReupload (627). If a push or direct upload of the same session is suspended in privateDB.save with a record prepared before the reanalysis, it resumes after markRemoved and calls markUploaded (Push:140 / 429); the queued uploadSession then sees the id as uploaded (394) and returns, so the reanalysed/repaired copy never reaches iCloud and other devices keep the old analysis.

flags.text: Uses wall-clock age since the sync began, while the body watchdog deliberately allows slow-but-progressing syncs to exceed 120 s. A second performFullSync call during a healthy long sync declares it stuck, shows 'Previous sync timed out' and clears syncingStartedAt while the original keeps running; the new call then waits in the serializer and runs another full sync.
